name: Temporary Residence for Investment/Entrepreneurial Activity (Law 200/2010 Art. 31, 36-1)

requirements.blocker_text: Investment of 30-200 times the average monthly salary in the economy, creating at least 1 job, confirmed by an auditor, with the company registered at the Public Services Agency (ASP). Grants a 2-year permit.
requirements.fix_path: Register a company and make the qualifying investment.

requirements.blocker_text: Investment of 4,000+ times the average monthly salary in the economy, creating at least 50 jobs. Grants an 8-year permit.
requirements.fix_path: Register a company and make the qualifying investment.

outcome.duration_length: 2 to 8 years depending on investment tier (30-200 salaries/1 job = 2yr; 200-600/8 jobs = 3yr; 600-2,000/15 jobs = 4yr; 2,000-4,000/25 jobs = 5yr; 4,000+/50 jobs = 8yr)

sources.title: Invest Moldova Agency (state investment-promotion body) -- obtaining temporary residence via investment: 5-tier table of investment amount (in multiples of the average monthly salary in the economy) vs. jobs created vs. permit duration; 3,600 MDL file-examination fee

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Moldova). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- tier-1 sourced via Invest Moldova, the state investment-promotion agency. Only the entry and top investment tiers are modeled as separate requirement_groups (OR alternatives); the three intermediate tiers (200-600/8jobs/3yr, 600-2,000/15jobs/4yr, 2,000-4,000/25jobs/5yr) are disclosed in the outcome.duration_length field rather than built as their own groups, to avoid an overly fragmented file -- all five tiers are real and sourced from the same table. Investment thresholds are expressed as multiples of Moldova's average monthly salary (a periodically-updated national figure) rather than a fixed MDL amount, since Moldova has no national-variables tracking file in this dataset yet -- the multiplier itself is the modeled value, not a formula-resolved currency figure. Thresholds came from a government-agency FAQ page paraphrase, not a direct read of the Law 200/2010 statute article -- recommend cross-verifying the exact salary-multiple table against the primary legal text before treating these numbers as final.
